listings.meatEvidence: The farm's home page says it farms pork and beef sustainably, makes products in its own on-farm kitchen and butchery, and sells direct from the farm each Friday or by appointment (https://www.martinsridgefarm.com.au/).
listings.caveats: The site gives no street number or postcode. Its directions say to take the Martins Ridge Road turnoff, drive 500 m, turn right at the Martins Ridge Farm sign, and it is the first property on the left. The map pin needs checking. Corrected on verification: I opened the home and contact pages. The site is a JS-rendered page, so I read the text from the raw HTML. The home page says the farm raises pork and beef sustainably and sells direct from the farm each Friday 10am-4pm or by appointment, and that its farm gate is open to the public. The contact page gives the Martins Ridge Road directions in Conjola. The hours and products check out. The description was wrong in two places: it says 'near Milton' and 'family farm', and the site says neither. I rewrote it to stick to what the site says.

listings.name: Stockinpiggle Farm Produce

hours.note: Closed Sunday to Tuesday. A separate farm store at 2124 Stockinbingle Road has varying days and hours (see Facebook).

listings.hoursAsStated: Cootamundra store: closed Monday and Tuesday; Wednesday to Friday 2pm to 6pm; Saturday 9am to 1pm; closed Sunday.
listings.description: A family farm and free-range pig stud based at Stockinbingle that sells its own pork, beef, lamb and chicken from a store in Cootamundra.
listings.meatEvidence: The business's own site says its pastured pork, grass-fed beef, lamb, hogget and pastured chicken come from its family farm, and gives the store's address and hours. Visit Cootamundra (council tourism) says it sells direct to consumers and has a store in Cootamundra (https://stockinpiggle.com.au/, https://visitcootamundra.com.au/food-and-wine/stockinpiggle/).
listings.caveats: This store is in Cootamundra town, not on the farm. The postcode 2590 comes from the Visit Cootamundra page (council tourism), not the business site. The council page gives a phone number, but the business site does not, so phone is left null. The farm store at Stockinbingle is left out of the hours because its hours vary. Corrected on verification: I opened the business's own site (copyright 2026). It confirms the store at 18 Adams Street, Cootamundra, open Wed-Fri 2pm-6pm and Sat 9am-1pm, closed Sun-Tue. It names pastured pork, grass-fed beef, lamb, hogget and pastured chicken from its family farm. The Visit Cootamundra (council) page confirms the pig stud, direct-to-consumer sales and the Cootamundra store, and 2590 is the Cootamundra postcode shown on that council page. One fix to the description: 'near Cootamundra' is the researcher's inference. The council page places the farm at Stockinbingle, so the description now says that.

listings.name: Integrity Meats

listings.caveats: The shop's page does not name meat types. Those come from the farm's site. The shop is in Goulburn town, not on the farm (the farm is at Wombeyan Caves). listings.meatEvidence: VisitCanberra (ACT Government tourism) lists beef among the stalls and describes the market as a place to talk with your farmers about how your food is produced (https://visitcanberra.com.au/attractions/5db8e9a6904c07d94aff5247/braidwood-farmers-market).
listings.caveats: No exact times are given, so the hours days object is empty and the schedule is in the note. The postcode is not shown. It confirms the market is held in the National Theatre on Braidwood's main street (Wallace Street), opposite the bakery, on the first and third Saturday mornings of each month. It names beef among the stalls, along with fruit and veg, wine, cider, non-alcoholic drinks, preserves, jam, black garlic and honey, and calls it a place to chat with your farmers. I could not find an own site (the likely domains did not resolve), and the web search budget for this run was used up, so I could not check further. The site names the chicken and pork only as stock ('organic beef and chicken and regeneratively farmed pork') and never says they come from the founders' farms.
